rubric.why: The equation must show methane reacting with two molecules of chlorine.

rubric.why: Bright sunlight produces carbon and hydrogen chloride in the balanced equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct products and their coefficients.

items.followUp: Define a molecular formula and give the molecular and empirical formulas of hydrogen peroxide.

rubric.why: A molecular formula gives the actual number of each type of atom in one molecule.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that it shows the actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule.

rubric.why: An empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for defining it as the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element.

rubric.why: Glucose provides a correct molecular-formula and empirical-formula example pair.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving glucose as C₆H₁₂O₆ with empirical formula CH₂O.

modelAnswer: A molecular formula shows the actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule of a compound.
For example, the molecular formula of glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆.
An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.
The empirical formula of glucose is CH₂O.

items.followUp: Explain the formation of an ionic bond between magnesium and oxygen, showing the ions formed.

rubric.why: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining an ionic bond as the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

rubric.why: A sodium atom loses one electron to form a sodium ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating or showing that sodium loses one electron and forms Na⁺.

rubric.why: A chlorine atom gains the electron and forms a chloride ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating or showing that chlorine gains one electron and forms Cl⁻.

rubric.why: The sodium and chloride ions have opposite charges, attract each other, and form sodium chloride.
rubric.description: Ions attract to form sodium chloride
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for identifying Na⁺ and Cl⁻ and explaining that their attraction forms ionic NaCl.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by transfer of electron(s).
A sodium atom has the electronic arrangement 2,8,1 and loses one electron: Na → Na⁺ + e⁻.
A chlorine atom has the electronic arrangement 2,8,7 and gains that electron: Cl + e⁻ → Cl⁻.
The Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions attract each other and form sodium chloride, NaCl.

items.followUp: Define solubility and state how increasing temperature affects the solubility of solids and gases in water.

rubric.why: Solubility specifies the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a given mass of solvent at a specified temperature to form a saturated solution.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for defining solubility as the maximum amount of solute dissolving in 100 g of solvent to form a saturated solution at a specified temperature.

rubric.why: The solubility of most solid substances in water increases with temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that increasing temperature generally increases the solubility of solids.

rubric.why: The solubility of gases in water generally decreases with temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that increasing temperature generally decreases the solubility of gases.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in 100 g of solvent to form a saturated solution at a specified temperature.
The solubility of most solid substances in water increases as the temperature increases.
The solubility of gases in water generally decreases as the temperature increases.

items.followUp: Define organic chemistry and give one example of an organic compound.

rubric.why: Organic chemistry is the study of hydrocarbons and their derivatives.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining organic chemistry as the study of hydrocarbons and their derivatives.

rubric.why: Methane is a correct example of an organic compound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving methane or its formula, CH₄.

modelAnswer: Organic chemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with hydrocarbons and their derivatives.
Methane (CH₄) is an example of an organic compound.
